description: We are  a team of six Grade 9 students and DECI alumni competing in NASA Space Apps 2026. Blending foundations in Python, HTML/CSS, and hardware prototyping with custom digital art, UI design, and storytelling, we turn complex NASA data into clear, interactive, and visually compelling experiences.
summary: Space Adventure is an interactive website for kids aged 10 to 14 that tells the stories of seven NASA machines left on the Moon. Visitors spin a 3D Moon, tap a machine such as Surveyor 3, the Apollo 11 lander Eagle, the lunar rover or an Apollo science instrument, and hear it tell its story in its own voice. They can then play games and take a quiz to earn stars. It answers the challenge by turning hardware that went quiet into friendly stories that connect each machine’s design to the science it made possible. It matters because this challenge touched our hearts, and because young people mostly hear about active missions, so they miss how much these older machines gave us and how they paved the way for future exploration.
details:
About Space Adventure

Space Adventure brings seven NASA machines left on the Moon between 1967 and 1972 to life. Visitors can spin an interactive 3D Moon and select a machine to open its dedicated page, featuring key facts, a NASA photo, and unique spoken narration. Giving each machine its own voice makes them truly feel alive. Navigating the 3D Moon offers a realistic sense of exploring the lunar surface, making the overall experience feel like an exciting adventure.

Features & Accessibility

The platform is free, requires no account, and works seamlessly on both computers and mobile devices. Its welcoming and user-friendly design is tailored for ages 10 to 14. Audio narration enhances engagement for children while offering crucial support for early readers and individuals with reading difficulties or low vision. Beyond exploring the Moon, the site features a timeline, comparison table, quiz, and interactive games like a jump game, matching game, and "guess the machine" game. User progress is saved in the browser and rewarded with stars and stickers.

Our Mission

We aim to help children have fun while learning about these historical spacecraft and their lasting impact on our world. Our goal is to forge a meaningful connection between young learners and these often-overlooked machines by letting landers and cameras from decades ago share their own stories.

Tools, Languages, & Technologies

  • Development & Graphics: VS Code, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js (used for rendering the 3D Moon).
  • Audio & Content: Spoken narrations were generated via Google Studio using scripts authored by our team.
  • AI Assistance: AI tools supported developers in adding the 3D Moon, debugging code, testing site functionality, fact-checking information, and writing the documentation. ( ChatGPT , Claude, Google Studio)

Presentation: The slide presentation utilizes a template from Slidesgo.
